title: The cuspidal cubic cone has a non-torsion conductor defect
content: Let X_g be the cubic y^3-x^2z=0 containing the rational quartic C. On w=1 its coordinate ring is A=k[z,za^2,za^3], with normalization B=k[z,za,za^2,za^3]. Using z=V^3, tau=UV^2, y=U^2V, x=U^3, the lift of C is U=V^4. Hence F=(U-V^4)^3=x-3yz+3 tau z^2-z^4 cuts out 3 C-tilde on the normalization. Since H=3R and C-tilde=4R, this realizes 3 C-tilde=4H. The conductor preimage is the double line Gamma=(x,y,tau^2). Restricting F gives -z^4(1-3 tau/z^2). Modulo pullbacks from the reduced conductor line, this has additive polar part -3 z^{-2} in W=z^{-1}k[z^{-1}], which is nonzero and torsion-free in characteristic zero. Therefore no positive multiple of 3C-4H vanishes in APic(X_g), and C is not an STCI on this cone.
significance: Exhibits an explicit obstruction invisible on the normalization: the divisor classes are proportional there, but the required relation fails to descend across the nonreduced conductor.
assumptions: The base field is algebraically closed of characteristic zero
Hartshorne-Polini's normalization-conductor exact sequence and identification of W apply
source_material: Craighero-Gattazzo's theorem for all cubic surfaces

relations.explanation: Computes the APic proportionality obstruction on one explicit singular containing surface.
The residual doubled singular line is reflected by a nonzero additive conductor class.
Separates normalization proportionality from conductor descent.

provenance.objective: Determine whether the rational quartic can become proportional to a hyperplane in APic of its cuspidal cubic cone.
provenance.method: Normalize by adjoining the missing Veronese monomial, construct the Cartier function for 3 C-tilde on a cyclic cover, and restrict it to the double-line conductor.
provenance.reasoning_summary: The class relation succeeds on the normalization, but its descent datum has nonzero polar part in a characteristic-zero additive group, so no multiple can kill it.
